title: Rolling Slice Simulator and Emergency De-scope Playbook
creator: Jared Kim
description: Problem: During mid-cycle shifts we repeatedly ran out of engineered capacity for Dedicated and Private rollout work and made ad-hoc scope cuts that degraded planned OKR outcomes. We lack a lightweight simulator and a codified decision matrix to: 1) model staffing/skill constraints against planned work slices, 2) run 'what-if' surge scenarios, and 3) execute a transparent, pre-approved emergency de-scope sequence.
objectives: Provide a rolling-slice simulator that models engineer availability, cross-functional dependencies, and slip propagation
Define a deterministic emergency de-scope protocol with triggers, owner handoffs, and communications templates
Reduce mid-cycle scope churn and improve predictability of shipped OKR key results
success_metrics: Reduce emergency scope cuts after week 2 of cycle by 50%
Decrease overall scope churn (stories moved out mid-cycle) by 30% vs prior cycle
90% of de-scopes follow the playbook decisions and communication template
deliverables: A minimal web-based rolling-slice simulator (spreadsheet import + UI) with a show/follow mode
A written Emergency De-scope Playbook (triggers, ranked cut list, fallback paths, comms) in Confluence
One runbook-run workshop with PMs/Eng/Design to validate thresholds and ranked-cut lists
Dashboards to track live staffing burn and projected completion probability by slice
out_of_scope: Full-time resource management / HR-level scheduling (we'll consume exported availability feeds)
Automated schedule changes without human approval
acceptance_criteria: Simulator ingests Cycle CSV export and produces a slice-level risk score and projected delivery date
Playbook documents clear triggers (utilization %, unblocked work aging) and a ranked de-scope list per initiative
Workshop completed with sign-off from at least 3 engineering leads and 2 PM leads
Dashboard surfaces projected KRs at risk and maps them to candidate de-scopes
steps: Draft initial simulator CSV schema and import adapter (week 0)
Prototype simulator UI and run 3 historical cycles through it to validate outputs (week 1)
Produce ranked de-scope catalogs for three high-impact initiatives and iterate with leads (week 2)
Ship Confluence playbook, run workshop, and onboard PMs to the simulator (week 3)
Monitor pilot during current cycle and collect feedback for iteration (ongoing)
